summary: 燧石矛尖和带刮痕的骨头证实人类猎过洞熊，骨骼分析又显示，以植物为主食使它们易受冰期影响。种群衰退早于气候变化，人类占据可供冬眠的洞穴，可能是促成灭绝的最后一击。
logic: 从洞内骨骼和绘画提出人熊关系问题
用矛尖和刮痕证实狩猎
从食性检验冰期缺粮解释
比较种群衰退与气候变化的时间

paragraphs.brief: 用骨骼化学成分重建生活史
sentences: Hervé Bocherens, an evolutionary biologist at the University of Tübingen, Germany, says his colleagues find his research methods a little ‘crude’.
德国图宾根大学的演化生物学家埃尔韦·博舍朗说，同事们觉得他的研究方法有点“粗暴”。

He dissolves 30,000-year-old animal bones in hydrochloric acid, which is strong enough to burn through metal, soaks the bone solution in lye, cooks it at about 200 degrees Fahrenheit and freeze-dries it, until what’s left is a speck of powder weighing less than one one-hundredth of an ounce.
他把三万年前的动物骨头溶于足以腐蚀金属的盐酸中，再用碱液浸泡，约在华氏二百度下加热，最后冻干，得到的粉末还不到百分之一盎司。
The method may be harsh, but the yield is precious – the biography of a cave bear as told through its chemical components.
手段虽粗暴，收获却珍贵：骨头里的化学成分可以讲述一头洞熊的生平。
Bocherens is at the forefront of research on the bear, a European species that died out 25,000 years ago.
洞熊生活在欧洲，约两万五千年前灭绝，博舍朗是研究它的前沿学者。

People have been excavating cave bear remains for hundreds of years— in the Middle Ages, the massive skulls were attributed to dragons — but the past decade has seen a burst of discoveries about how the bears lived and why they became extinct.
几个世纪以来人们一直在发掘洞熊遗骸，中世纪的人甚至把硕大的头骨当成龙骨；近十年才接连出现有关洞熊生活和灭绝的新发现。
An abundance of bones has been found from Spain to Romania in caves where the animals once hibernated.
从西班牙到罗马尼亚，人们在洞熊曾经冬眠的山洞里找到了大量骨骼。
‘Caves are good places to preserve bones, and cave bears had the good sense to die there,’ Bocherens says.
博舍朗风趣地说：“山洞很适合保存骨头，洞熊倒挺会挑地方，死在了洞里。”
paragraphs.gist: 研究者从洞穴里保存的古熊骨提取微量化学成分，以重建这种约两万五千年前灭绝的欧洲巨兽的生活史。

paragraphs.brief: 巨型洞熊与人类关系之谜
sentences: Along with mammoths, lions and woolly rhinos, cave bears (Ursus spelaeus) were once among Europe’s most impressive creatures.
洞熊曾和猛犸象、狮子、披毛犀一样，是欧洲最壮观的动物之一。
Males weighed up to 1,500 pounds, 50 per cent more than the largest modern grizzly bears.
雄性熊的重量高达1500磅，比现代最大的灰熊高出50%.
Cave bears had wider heads than today’s bears, and powerful shoulders and forelimbs.
洞熊的头部比现生熊类宽，肩膀和前肢都很强壮。
But the relationship between humans and cave bears has been mysterious.
但人类和洞熊之间的关系一直很神秘
Were humans prey for the bears, or predators?
对于洞熊来说，人类到底是猎物，还是猎手？
Were bears the object of worship or fear?
人类对洞熊是崇拜，还是畏惧？
paragraphs.gist: 洞熊体型巨大、前肢有力，人类是否曾捕食它们、被它们猎食或把它们当作崇拜对象，却长期缺少清晰答案。

paragraphs.brief: 洞穴画、熊骨与祭祀疑问
sentences: Initially cave bears shared the continent of Europe, more than 100,000 years ago, with Neanderthals, a primitive species of humans.
十多万年前，与洞熊同在欧洲生活的是一种古人类——尼安德特人。
Modern humans arrived in Europe about 40,000 years ago, and were soon aware of the bears.
现代人类大约在四万年前来到欧洲不久就意识到了熊的存在
They painted images of the animals on cave walls, and carved their likeness in fragments of mammoth tusk.
他们在洞壁上画洞熊，也用猛犸象的象牙碎片雕出它们的形象。
The walls of France’s Chauvet cave are painted with lions, hyenas and bears; dating back 32,000 years, these are perhaps the oldest paintings in the world.
法国肖维岩洞壁上绘有狮子、鬣狗和熊，距今约 3.2 万年，可能是世界上最古老的绘画作品。
The painters weren’t the cave’s only occupants: the floor is covered with 150 cave bear skeletons, and its soft clay still holds paw prints.
到过这里的还有洞熊：洞底散布着约一百五十具洞熊骨架，柔软的黏土上仍留有爪印。
Most dramatically, a cave bear skull was perched on a stone slab in the center of one chamber, placed deliberately by some long-gone cave inhabitant.
最引人注目的是，有人曾刻意把一颗洞熊头骨放在一间洞室中央的石板上。
‘There’s no way to tell if it was just curiosity that made someone put a skull on the rock, or if it had religious significance,’ says Bocherens.
博舍朗说，无法判断摆放头骨的人是一时好奇，还是赋予了它某种宗教意义。
paragraphs.gist: 肖维洞穴同时保留有人类绘画、熊骨和爪印，岩台上刻意放置的熊颅尤其引人注目，但其举动有无宗教含义难以确定。

paragraphs.brief: 德国洞穴的人熊越冬痕迹
sentences: Another discovery, hundreds of miles to the east of Chauvet, would shed light on the relationship between cave bears and humans.
肖维岩洞以东数百英里的另一处发现，让人们进一步了解了洞熊与人类的关系。
The Swabian Jura is a limestone plateau in southwestern Germany that is riddled with caves.
德国西南部的施瓦本汝拉是一片遍布洞穴的石灰岩高原。
A steel gate guards the Hohle Fels cave from vandals and curiosity-seekers.
一道钢门挡住了想进霍勒费尔斯洞穴破坏或猎奇的人。
Floodlights in the cave’s main chamber illuminate the ceiling, vaulted like a cathedral above 5,000 square feet of floor space.
泛光灯照亮了主洞室的顶部，它像大教堂的穹顶一样，覆盖着五千平方英尺的地面。
Long ago, as shown by the bones and tools that archaeologists have found, cave bears and human beings sought shelter here from winter weather.
考古学家发现的骨头和工具表明，很久以前洞熊和人类都曾来此躲避严冬。
paragraphs.gist: 德国霍勒费尔斯洞穴出土的骨骼和工具显示，人类与洞熊都曾在那里躲避寒冬，为研究双方关系提供了另一处现场。

sentences: In 2000, University of Tübingen paleobiologist Susanne Münzel unearthed a bear vertebra with a tiny triangular piece of flint embedded in it.
2000年，图宾根大学古生物学家Susanne Münzel 挖出了一只熊脊椎，其中嵌有一块小的三角火石。
The flint was likely a broken spear point, hard evidence of a successful bear hunt 29,000 years ago.
这块燧石很可能是折断的矛尖，是人类在两万九千年前成功猎熊的确凿证据。
paragraphs.gist: 一块熊椎骨中嵌着可能是矛尖碎片的燧石，为约两万九千年前人类成功猎熊提供了直接证据。

paragraphs.brief: 石器切痕证明取肉行为
sentences: Münzel also found bear bones that had clearly been scraped by stone tools.
Münzel还发现了明显被石器刮伤的熊骨头。
Evidence for bears being a food source for early humans was shown by cut marks on skulls and leg bones where the flesh had been cut away.
头骨和腿骨上有割肉留下的切痕，说明早期人类曾以熊肉为食。
Many of the bones were from baby bears, perhaps caught while hibernating.
许多骨头都是来自小熊可能是在冬眠时被抓住的
paragraphs.gist: 头骨和腿骨上用石器割肉的痕迹表明洞熊曾是食物，许多骨骼来自幼熊，它们可能在冬眠时被捕。

paragraphs.brief: 同位素揭示以植物为主的饮食
sentences: Cave bears disappeared not long after humans spread throughout Europe, and one theory is that hunting led to the bears’ extinction.
人类遍布欧洲后不久，洞熊就消失了；一种观点认为人类狩猎造成了洞熊灭绝。
Hervé Bocherens’ test tubes may hold the clues.
博舍朗的试管里或许藏着线索。

Running his white powder through a mass spectrometer, he identifies different isotopes, or chemical forms, of elements such as carbon and nitrogen that reflect what the bears were eating and how quickly they grew.
他用质谱仪分析白色粉末，辨认碳、氮等元素的不同同位素，由此推断洞熊吃什么、长得有多快。
After studying hundreds of bones from dozens of sites in Europe, Bocherens has found that cave bears ate mainly plants.
在研究了欧洲几十处遗址的数百块骨头之后，Bocherens发现洞熊主要吃植物。
paragraphs.gist: 研究者用质谱仪测定欧洲各地数百块熊骨的碳、氮同位素，以推断生长和饮食，其中的共同特征显示洞熊主要吃植物。

paragraphs.brief: 冰期改变植被与熊群迁移
sentences: This would have made bears particularly vulnerable to the last Ice Age, which began around 30,000 years ago.
这将使熊特别容易受到30 000年前开始的最后一个冰河时代的影响。
This Ice Age shortened or eliminated growing seasons, and altered the distributions of plant species across Europe.
这一冰河时代缩短或消除了生长季节，改变了欧洲各地植物物种的分布。
Cave bears began to move from their old territories, according to a DNA analysis of teeth found near the Danube River.
根据对多瑙河附近发现的牙齿进行的DNA分析，洞穴熊开始从老地方移走。
The cave bear population there was relatively stable, with the same genetic patterns showing up generation after generation.
这一地区的洞熊种群原本相当稳定，一代代洞熊呈现相同的遗传特征。
But about 28,000 years ago, newcomers with different DNA patterns arrived — a possible sign of hungry bears suddenly on the move.
但约两万八千年前出现了遗传特征不同的外来洞熊，这可能意味着饥饿突然迫使洞熊迁移。
paragraphs.gist: 冰期缩短植物生长季、改变植被分布，多瑙河附近约两万八千年前突然出现不同遗传特征的个体，或是洞熊因饥饿而迁移的迹象。

paragraphs.brief: 缺少冬眠洞穴可能加速灭绝
sentences: But changes in the climate can’t be solely to blame for the bears’ extinction.
洞熊灭绝不能完全归咎于气候变化。

According to the latest study, by Erik Trinkaus and his colleagues at the Max Planck Institute, cave bear populations began a long, slow decline 50,000 years ago — well before the climate began to change.
据马克斯·普朗克研究所的埃里克·特林考斯及同事的最新研究，洞熊数量早在五万年前就开始长期缓慢下降，比气候变化早得多。
The new study supports a different explanation for the cave bears’ demise.
这项研究支持对洞熊灭绝的另一种解释。
As Neanderthals, and then a growing population of modern humans moved into the caves of Europe, cave bears had fewer safe places to hibernate.
尼安德特人以及随后数量日增的现代人相继进入欧洲的洞穴，使洞熊可安全冬眠的场所越来越少。
An acute housing shortage may have been the final blow for these magnificent beasts.
严重缺少栖身之所，可能给了这些壮硕的动物最后一击。
paragraphs.gist: 洞熊数量在明显气候转变前就已开始下降，研究者提出尼安德特人及现代人占用洞穴，可能让洞熊失去安全的冬眠场所。

items.en: Bocherens’ findings on cave bears involve measuring the length of complete bones.
items.zh: Bocherens对山洞熊的发现涉及测量完整的骨头长度。
items.why: 题干说“测量完整骨骼长度”,而文中描述的是把骨头溶解并做化学分析/ 同位素分析，不是测量完整骨骼长度，故与原文矛盾。

items.en: Bocherens was the first person to conduct analytical research on cave bears in a laboratory.
items.zh: Bocherens是第一个在实验室对洞熊进行分析研究的人。
items.why: 文中只说他“处在研究前沿 /领先*,并未说明他是第一位在实验室做分析研究的人。“first person” 无法从文中验证，故为NG。

items.en: Cave bears have been extinct for 25,000 years.
items.why: 作者把洞熊称为大约两万五千年前灭绝的欧洲物种，时间与题干相符。

items.en: At one time, people thought the excavated remains of bears were those of dragons.
items.zh: 人们一度把挖出的洞熊遗骸当作龙的遗骸。
items.why: 中世纪的人曾把出土的巨大洞熊头骨归给传说中的龙。

items.en: Modern grizzly bears are similar in size to cave bears.
items.zh: 现代灰熊的大小与洞熊相似。
items.why: 洞能比现代灰驴大50%,并非“大小相近/相似”,故与题干矛盾。

items.en: Neanderthals understood cave bear behaviour better than modern humans did.
items.zh: 尼安德特人比现代人更了解洞穴熊的行为
items.why: 文章交代尼安德特人与洞熊曾生活在同一片大陆，没有比较他们与现代人对洞熊行为了解多少。

items.en: Over a hundred ________ of cave bears, together with paw prints, were found on the floor of the cave.
items.zh: 人们在洞穴地面发现了一百多具洞熊的________，以及洞熊的爪印。
items.why: “超过一百具洞能骨架，并留有爪印”,与笔记一致。

items.en: The ________ of a cave bear was found in a prominent position in the cave.
items.zh: 在洞穴中一个显眼的位置，人们发现了一只洞熊的________。
items.why: “洞能的头骨被放在显眼位置 (洞室中央的石板上)”。

items.en: Bones and tools found in the cave indicate it provided ________ for both bears and humans.
items.zh: 洞穴里出土的骨骼和工具表明，熊和人类都曾在这里获得________。
items.why: Hohle Fels 洞鹤为人能提供避所/庇护。

items.en: Isotopes from the bones indicate that ________ were the cave bears’ preferred food.
items.zh: 骨骼中的同位素表明，洞熊最爱吃的是________。
items.why: 同位素显示洞能以植物为主食。

items.en: The Ice Age changed vegetation growth in ________
items.zh: 冰期改变了植被在不同________里的生长情况。
items.why: 回到对应内容“这一冰河时代缩短或消除了生长季节，改变了欧洲各地植物物种的分布”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Support for the above explanation comes from a study of changes in the DNA in the ________ of the population of cave bears near the Danube River at this time.
items.zh: 研究者分析了当时多瑙河附近洞熊种群的________中所含DNA的变化，结果支持上述解释。
items.why: 对靠近多瑙河发现的洞能牙齿做DNA 分析，为“气候导致迁徙”的证据来源。

items.en: Competition from Neanderthals and modern humans for caves may have reduced opportunities for cave bears to ________
items.zh: 尼安德特人和现代人与洞熊争夺洞穴，可能减少了洞熊________的机会。
items.why: 人口扩张占洞穴，洞能冬眠机会变少。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

pairs: 第 1 段 · 第 2 句
第 2 段 · 第 2 句
points: 洞能比现代灰驴大50%,并非“大小相近/相似”,故与题干矛盾。
回到对应内容“这一冰河时代缩短或消除了生长季节，改变了欧洲各地植物物种的分布”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: “that had clearly been scraped by stone tools”修饰前面的 bones。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 bones，再把修饰信息接回主句。
After studying hundreds of bones from dozens of sites in Europe, Bocherens has found ….
“that cave bears ate mainly plants”补足 found 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 found 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
